source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Telehealth practice is exempt from state nursing licensure whenever communication occurs remotely","B":"A home-state nursing license automatically authorizes practice in every other state by telehealth","C":"No state authorization matters when the encounter does not involve in-person nursing contact","D":"Practice authority generally must cover the state where the client is located during the encounter"}}
source_row.rationale: Absent specific compact or reciprocity arrangements, telehealth nursing practice is generally governed by the location of the client (patient) receiving care, meaning the nurse typically needs to hold licensure or otherwise meet the legal requirements of the state where the client is physically located at the time of the encounter — an important consideration given the interstate nature of telehealth.
source_row.source_detail: NCSBN telehealth/licensure principle: practice authority generally follows the patient location unless compact/other authority applies; reviewed 2026-08-14.
source_row.source_name: NCSBN — Telehealth Nursing Practice and Interstate Licensure Considerations
